topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The rain's like a relentless faucet, leaking into every crack, making everything feel heavier. I stand at the edge of the yard, enamel mug of cold coffee clutched in my hand, watching my neighbor, Thompson, amble over. He's got a way about him—too many smiles, too eager for favors. "Mind if I use a patch of your yard for a garden?" he asks, eyes flickering with something I can't quite pin. I eye the ground, the sparse, stubborn weeds fighting for life. Another player in the game, wanting a piece of the action. "Sure, Thompson," I say, voice hoarse. "Just make sure your roots don't run too deep."
